rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: a positional claim about another file that turns out wrong misleads the reader about what's coming next. Present here: chunk 0 line 9 states 'The compound move (writing down what you learned) lives in the next exercise.' M1's actual order (getting-going.md: orient-and-introspect -> fix-tests-first -> close-the-ticket -> compound-and-close) makes the immediate next exercise close-the-ticket (tracker-convention read + close-out note), not the compound move — that lives in compound-and-close, two exercises later. This file's own Arc backing-block entry ('Hands off to: close-the-ticket') confirms the contradiction. A student/trainer reading the title slide is set up to expect the very next block to be the compound step, and it isn't.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Drop the immediate-adjacency claim, e.g. 'The compound move (writing down what you learned) comes later in this module, once the ticket's closed' — or cut the positional claim entirely and let the Arc/hand-off note carry the sequencing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
Live-demo beats survive a text read.
Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
